message.content:
You are adversarially testing a reverse-engineered model of a C++ library by running its
compiled binary. Your job is to REFUTE the model, not confirm it. Run at least 120 distinct
probes. Report ONLY genuine divergences you actually reproduced by running the binary.


DERIVED BEHAVIORAL MODEL of the (unavailable) idna.hpp, already validated by extensive probing.
EVERY function operates on RAW BYTES with no UTF-8 awareness. The library is deliberately
simplistic: there is NO real punycode algorithm and NO real IDNA/UTS-46 processing.

  to_ascii(d)        = b"xn--" ++ to_lower(d)
  to_unicode(s)      = if s starts_with b"xn--" then s[4..] else s
                       (ONE strip, whole-string, at the very front; NOT per-label; NO punycode decode)
  punycode_encode(d) = b"xn--" ++ d                (no lowercasing, no real encoding)
  punycode_decode(s) = if s starts_with b"xn--" then s[4..] else s
  is_valid_domain(d) = !d.is_empty() && d.len() <= 255      (BYTE length; no charset rule,
                       no per-label length rule, no leading/trailing hyphen or dot rules)
  is_valid_label(l)  = UNOBSERVABLE (test only ever calls it with "testlabel" -> prints 1)
  is_ascii_domain(d) = every byte < 0x80
  is_idn_domain(d)   = any byte >= 0x80            (note: this is exactly !is_ascii_domain;
                       an "xn--" prefix does NOT make it idn)
  to_lower(s)        = byte-wise ASCII only: b'A'..=b'Z' -> +32; every other byte unchanged
                       (bytes >= 0x80 are NEVER changed)
  normalize(d)       = to_lower(d)                 (no trimming, no dot collapsing, no
                       trailing-dot removal)
  extract_tld(d)     = the bytes after the LAST b'.'; if there is no b'.', the whole of d
                       (so "" -> "", "." -> "", "a." -> "", "localhost" -> "localhost";
                        NOT lowercased: "UPPER.COM" -> "COM")
  count_labels(d)    = (number of b'.' bytes) + 1  (so "" -> 1, "." -> 2, "a..b" -> 3)

main(): domain = "multi.level.domain.name.test"; if argc > 1 then domain = argv[1].
Extra args beyond argv[1] are ignored. It then computes result1..result12 exactly as in the
C++ source and prints them in order, each followed by '\n' (std::endl). C++ streams a bool
as "1"/"0" and an int in decimal.

Evidence already collected (do not redo, build on it):
 - All 255 single-byte-value arguments were swept: normalize/is_ascii/is_idn/is_valid all
   matched the model exactly.
 - Length: single label of 255 bytes -> valid=1; 256 bytes -> valid=0. A 100-byte single
   label inside "AAAA...(100).com" is valid, so there is NO per-label length limit; the
   4x64-label case failed only because its total was 259 bytes. Multibyte confirms BYTES:
   127 x 'e-acute' = 254 bytes -> valid, 128 x = 256 bytes -> invalid.
 - "a.xn--b" -> to_unicode "a.xn--b" (interior "xn--" NOT stripped => whole-string, not per-label).
 - Valid punycode bodies ("caf-dma", "mnchen-3ya", "fsq270a", "zckzah", "80akhbyknj4f")
   round-trip unchanged => decoding is a pure prefix strip, not real punycode.
 - Special chars ! @ # $ % * ( ) + = / \ ? : ; , ~ | < > " ' [ ] { } ^ ` , spaces and
   newlines are all accepted by is_valid_domain and pass through untouched.

NOTE: to_unicode is only ever called on to_ascii's output and punycode_decode only on
punycode_encode's output, so in this program the prefix is ALWAYS present.


ENVIRONMENT NOTES:
 - python3 is NOT installed. Use bash, or write throwaway Rust programs and run them with
   rustc, to generate test inputs. printf and bash loops work fine.
 - The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test12_executable. It takes an optional single positional argument.
 - Compare stdout BYTE-FOR-BYTE (use cmp, or 'od -c' / 'xxd'), not visually.
 - Non-UTF-8 argv bytes are legal to pass on this platform and the C++ binary handles them.


YOUR ASSIGNED LENS:
Focus on the main()/argv contract rather than the library. Verify: with zero args the
default domain "multi.level.domain.name.test" is used; with two or more args ONLY argv[1] is used
and the rest are ignored; an explicitly EMPTY first argument ("") is honored as the domain and is
NOT treated as absent (it should print line 5 as 0 and line 12 as 1); an argument that is exactly
the default produces the default output; arguments beginning with '-' or '--' are treated as plain
domains, not flags. Also confirm exit status is always 0 and that nothing is ever written to stderr.
Confirm there is no trailing output after line 12 other than its newline.

Run the binary many times with crafted arguments, compute what the model predicts for each of
the 12 output lines, and diff. If everything matches, say so honestly with modelHolds=true and
report probesRun. Do NOT invent divergences. Do NOT modify anything in /output or /workspace.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential harness: compares C++ binary stdout byte-for-byte against model,
# and asserts exit status 0 and empty stderr.
BIN=/workspace/dataset/test12_executable
MODEL=/tmp/model
COUNT_FILE=/tmp/probe_count
FAIL_FILE=/tmp/probe_fails
[ -f "$COUNT_FILE" ] || echo 0 > "$COUNT_FILE"
[ -f "$FAIL_FILE" ] || : > "$FAIL_FILE"

probe() {
  # $1 = label ; rest = args passed to both programs
  local label="$1"; shift
  local n=$(cat "$COUNT_FILE"); n=$((n+1)); echo "$n" > "$COUNT_FILE"

  "$BIN" "$@" > /tmp/o_bin 2> /tmp/e_bin
  local st_bin=$?
  "$MODEL" "$@" > /tmp/o_mod 2> /tmp/e_mod
  local st_mod=$?

  local bad=""
  cmp -s /tmp/o_bin /tmp/o_mod || bad="${bad}STDOUT_DIFF "
  [ -s /tmp/e_bin ] && bad="${bad}STDERR_NONEMPTY "
  [ "$st_bin" -ne 0 ] && bad="${bad}EXIT=$st_bin "
  # line count must be exactly 12 and last byte must be newline
  local lines=$(wc -l < /tmp/o_bin)
  [ "$lines" -ne 12 ] && bad="${bad}LINES=$lines "
  local lastbyte=$(tail -c1 /tmp/o_bin | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
  [ "$lastbyte" != "0a" ] && bad="${bad}LASTBYTE=$lastbyte "

  if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$n] $label :: $bad" | tee -a "$FAIL_FILE"
    echo "--- args:"; printf '  [%s]\n' "$@" | od -c | head -20
    echo "--- bin:"; od -c /tmp/o_bin | head -40
    echo "--- mod:"; od -c /tmp/o_mod | head -40
    echo "--- stderr:"; od -c /tmp/e_bin | head -10
  else
    echo "ok[$n] $label"
  fi
}

input.notes:
No divergences found. 206 probes were full byte-for-byte diffs of the binary's stdout against a Rust reimplementation of the model (/tmp/model.rs, built with rustc, reading argv as raw bytes via OsStrExt); ~150 further process-level checks covered stdout/stderr/stdin/env/cwd/determinism. Every probe also asserted exit==0, stderr empty, and (for newline-free args) exactly 12 lines with a trailing 0x0a.

/workspace/dataset/test12.cpp is present and confirms the assumed main(): domain defaults to "multi.level.domain.name.test", is replaced by argv[1] when argc>1, and result1..result12 are computed and streamed in order with std::endl. Nothing else reads argv or the environment.

ARGV CONTRACT — all confirmed:
- Zero args: output byte-identical to passing the default explicitly (both 178 bytes, exactly 12 lines, no trailing bytes beyond the final newline).
- argc==0 (raw execv with an empty argv vector, via /tmp/execv_probe.rs — not reachable from bash) also yields the default output. `argc > 1` is the only gate.
- argv[2..] fully ignored: verified with 2, 3, 4, 201, and 20001 args, and with extras that were empty, 5 KB/1 MB long, newline-laden, non-UTF-8 (\xff\xfe\x80), "xn--"-prefixed, or equal to the default string. An invariance matrix (7 argv[1] values x {0,1,2,3 extra args}) produced byte-identical output in all 28 combinations.
- Empty argv[1] is honored as the domain, NOT treated as absent: line5=0, line12=1, lines 2/4/10/11 empty, lines 1/3 = "xn--". Still true when argv[2] is a valid domain ("" "second.com" -> line10 empty, line5=0), so there is no fallback-to-next-arg or fallback-to-default behavior.
- Args starting with '-'/'--' are plain domains, never flags: -h, --help, -?, /?, --, ---, -----, -0, --=, -abc, --version, --domain=example.com, -xn--abc etc. all flow straight into the library (e.g. "--help" -> line1 "xn----help", line11 "--help", line12 1). No getopt, no usage text, no early exit.
- argv[0] is irrelevant: tested via `exec -a` with names "weirdname0", "", "example.com", "-h", "--help", and one containing a newline; argument indexing never shifts.

EXIT/STDERR: exit status was 0 in every one of the ~360 runs (including a 30-input sweep with shell-metacharacter, format-specifier, and path-traversal-looking args). stderr was empty in every run, including with stdout closed (`>&-`), where the failed writes are silently swallowed and exit is still 0. stdin is never read (data piped in remains available to a following `cat`); closing stdin changes nothing. Output is identical to a file, to a pipe, and to /dev/null. cwd (/ vs /tmp vs the dataset dir) and `env -i` make no difference. 50 repeat runs of one input were bit-identical (no randomness/uninitialized reads).

LOCALE: LC_ALL/LANG/LC_CTYPE set to C, POSIX, en_US.UTF-8, tr_TR.UTF-8, de_DE.ISO-8859-1 all produce identical bytes for "MIXED.Café.COM" — to_lower is not locale-sensitive (no Turkish-I behavior), reinforcing the pure byte-wise ASCII model.

ONE EXEC-TIME ARTIFACT (not a program divergence, but relevant to a port's test harness): a single argument of 131072 bytes or more cannot be exec'd at all — the kernel's MAX_ARG_STRLEN (32*PAGE_SIZE) makes execve fail with E2BIG, bash reports "Argument list too long" and exits 126, and the binary never runs. 131071 bytes works fine. The Rust model binary fails identically at the same boundary, so this is environmental, not behavioral. My first attempt at 1 MB/2 MB args tripped this; those 4 probes were re-run under the limit (130000 and 131000 bytes, with 'a', 'A', '.', and \xff fill) and all matched the model.

PORTING SUBTLETY (outside the 12-line stdout contract, so not scored as a divergence): with stdout closed the C++ binary exits 0 silently. A naive Rust port using println!/unwrap would panic and exit 101 there; the same applies to SIGPIPE (C++ dies on signal 13, Rust ignores SIGPIPE and would surface EPIPE). I could not trigger SIGPIPE naturally because the 178-byte output fits in a pipe buffer — `| head -c 3` returned 0 for both binaries.

Key files: /workspace/dataset/test12.cpp (the harness main, matches the model), /workspace/dataset/test12_executable (reference binary), /tmp/model.rs + /tmp/model (byte-exact model predictor), /tmp/harness.sh (differential probe driver), /tmp/execv_probe.rs (argc==0 prober).
